verdicts.note: Not a lone ESSB 6346 vote: nay on 6346 (2026-03-09), ESHB 2081 and ESSB 5814 (2025) [S6][S7][S8], plus two 2026 statements against the income tax and for lower tax burdens [S4][S5] and the statement's 'reducing tax burdens' [S1]. Roll calls checked against the cached XML.

Repeated statement, verified in both releases: the operating budget has 'roughly doubled' / 'more than doubled' in a decade and the state should manage existing revenue first [S4][S5]; 'fiscally responsible' limited government [S1].

Both votes point to pole_a: yea on E2SHB 1110 middle housing (supply/deregulation; 2023-03-06 and 2023-04-18) and nay on EHB 1217 rent-increase cap (passage and conference report, 2025) [S10][S11]. Votes only, no statement on housing policy beyond 'no meaningful' affordability bills [S5], so medium is right. (The 1217 roll call also shows a yea on a 2025-04-23 'Concur in Senate amendments' motion before the bill went to conference; it does not change the final-passage direction.)
Nay on final passage of ESHB 1054 and E2SHB 1310 (2021) [S13][S14] and the 2026 statement on repeat offenders [S5]: record plus statement.

The only climate evidence is one 2021 nay vote on the Climate Commitment Act [S12]; the dossier says no campaign statement on climate was found. A single vote against creating the program is clear on direction but does not show the full pole_a position (repeal or paring back the CCA, gas taxes); by analogy with the single-vote rule for taxes, magnitude 1 at medium.

Nay on ESHB 1469 (2023), the reproductive and gender-affirming care shield law, verified in the cached roll call [S15], plus Life Choices of Yakima (a pregnancy center) in his own statement's community service [S1]. Both are reproductive/gender evidence, not schools evidence; medium is right for a vote plus an affiliation.

His statement names 'parental rights' [S1]; two nay votes on ESHB 1296 (2025-03-12, 2025-04-24) [S9]; 2026 criticism of the Legislature for refusing hearings on the parental-rights initiative [S5]. All parents-and-schools evidence; record plus repeated statements supports high.
One 2019 nay on E2SSB 5497 (Keep Washington Working) [S16], no statement; -1 medium already reflects a single vote.

Current 2026 statement 'We deserve universal health care' [S1] plus 2020 'Washington state could provide universal healthcare' and criticism of job-tied coverage [S2], both verified. 'State could provide' points to public coverage; campaign statements only, so medium rather than high.

The 2026 statement says 'Investment in our future is the way to transform our home' and calls for youth skills programs and need-based college/vocational access [S1]; +1 rather than +2 is appropriate for general language.

The only climate evidence is a single 2020 interview line ('one of the existential threats to society', 'listen to science') [S2], six years old and from a different campaign, with no policy attached; the 2026 statement says only 'Science and ability to Compromise are required' [S1]. Direction is plausible but the evidence is dated and indirect, so low.
No government office [S1]; his statement argues against 'the same faces and ideas' [S1]. Prior unsuccessful runs (2018, 2020) [S2] do not make an officeholder record.
